chunks: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa narrated to us. He said: al-Qasim b. Yahya narrated to us from his grandfather al-Hasan b. Rashid from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as). He said:

If a man is wronged and he continues to pray against the one who wronged him, Allah, exalted is His majesty, says: 'Indeed, here is another who is praying against you, alleging that you wronged him. If you wish, I will answer your prayer and answer his prayer against you. And if you wish, I will delay both of you, and My forgiveness will encompass you both.'

key_terms.أَخَّرْتُكُمَا: I delay both of you — divine postponement favoring mercy over immediate retribution
key_terms.ظُلِمَ: is wronged — passive voice indicating oppression
key_terms.عَفْوِي: My forgiveness — Allah's encompassing pardon that transcends human grievances

ai.seo_question: What does Allah say when a wronged person prays against their oppressor?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) reports that when a wronged man prays against his oppressor, Allah responds by noting that the oppressor himself is also being prayed against by someone he wronged. Allah then offers two choices: to answer both prayers (which would mean both are punished), or to delay judgment and encompass both parties with His forgiveness. This hadith reveals the depth of divine mercy, showing that Allah prefers forgiveness over retribution even when justice is sought.
word_analysis: and it will encompass you both

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us. He said: Al-Qasim b. Yahya narrated to us from his grandfather al-Hasan b. Rashid from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:

If a man is wronged and he prays against the one who wronged him, Allah says: “Here is one who prays against you, alleging that you have wronged him. If I wish, I could come to your aid or I could grant his prayer against you, or if I wish, I could delay it and encompass the both of you with My forgiveness.”
